title: Spotting a phishing message
summary: Phishing tricks you into revealing passwords, OTPs or money by pretending to be someone you trust.
keyPoints: Genuine organisations never ask for your password, PIN, CVV or OTP.
Hover over links before tapping - the real address is what matters, not the text.
Urgency ('act now', 'account will be blocked') is a pressure tactic.
Check the sender address, not just the display name.
redFlags: Unexpected message about an account problem
A link to 'verify' or 'update' details
Spelling and grammar mistakes
A reply-to address different from the sender

title: UPI and QR code safety
summary: Scanning a QR or approving a UPI request always sends money OUT of your account - never in.
keyPoints: You never scan a QR to RECEIVE money, a refund or a reward.
A 'collect request' pulls money from you - decline unless you started it.
Check the payee name and amount on the confirmation screen every time.
Verify a merchant's UPI ID from their official app or website.
redFlags: Someone says 'scan this to get your refund/cashback'
A pre-filled large amount you did not enter
A QR sticker pasted over another one
Payee name looks like a business but the UPI ID is personal

title: OTP and card-detail fraud
summary: An OTP is the last line of defence for your money. Anyone asking for it is a fraudster.
keyPoints: No bank, wallet, delivery agent or official ever needs your OTP.
Do not read out card number, expiry or CVV to callers.
Fraudsters create urgency so you share the code before thinking.
If you shared an OTP, call your bank immediately to block the account.
redFlags: 'Share the code we just sent to confirm your identity'
Caller claims to be from your bank's 'security team'
Pressure to act before an account is 'blocked'

title: Recognising a fake website
summary: Scam sites copy a brand's look but live on a slightly different address.
keyPoints: Read the domain carefully: 'paypa1.com' is not 'paypal.com'.
A padlock (HTTPS) only means the connection is encrypted, not that the site is honest.
Type important addresses yourself instead of following links.
Be wary of login pages reached from an email or SMS link.
redFlags: Look-alike or misspelled domain
Site asks for full card details plus OTP on one page
Newly created domain with a well-known brand name
Pop-up claiming your device is infected

title: The 'digital arrest' scam
summary: Callers pose as police, CBI or customs and claim you are involved in a crime to extort money.
keyPoints: Law enforcement never arrests or fines anyone over a call or video chat.
No agency asks you to stay on a call or transfer money to 'clear your name'.
Hang up, do not share documents, and report to the cyber-crime helpline (1930 in India).
Tell an elderly family member about this scam - it targets them most.
redFlags: 'Your Aadhaar/parcel is linked to a money-laundering case'
'Do not disconnect the call or tell anyone'
Demand for a 'refundable' verification transfer
Video call with someone in a uniform / fake office

title: Task, job and prize scams
summary: You are promised easy earnings or a prize, then asked to pay a fee you never get back.
keyPoints: A real employer does not ask you to pay a registration or deposit fee.
'Like and rate' task jobs on Telegram/WhatsApp are money-laundering fronts.
You cannot win a lottery you never entered.
Small early 'payouts' are bait to get a bigger deposit from you.
redFlags: Upfront fee, deposit or 'training kit' payment
Recruitment entirely over WhatsApp/Telegram
Guaranteed daily income for trivial work
Pressure to recruit friends
